title: Assurance fingerprint notes - quick scratch
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for SOC2 control mapping and evidence ideas. Not polished — capture fast, iterate.

High-level assumptions (for this sprint):
- Focus: CC (common criteria) around access, change mgmt, incident response, logging, and vendor mgmt.
- Target audit window: Jan 2026 - Mar 2026 (demo-ready by end-Apr).
- Evidence must be sliceable per service (hosted api / dedicated / private).

Open questions (need to resolve before owner reviews):
1) How do we represent ephemeral infra access? - contractors/infra-temp keys: do we capture ephemeral tokens in IAM logs or require ticket references? Need policy text + ticketing crosswalk.
2) Encryption at rest: some private deployments bring their own KMS — should we treat as "customer-managed" and document boundary, or require proof of customer KMS policies?
3) Backup retention variance across regions — default 30d, some regs want 90d. We need exceptions table.

Quick control mapping draft (very rough):
- Access controls (AC): IAM roles, SSO logs, MFA enforcement, PAM for privileged ops. Evidence: IAM policy snapshots, SSO login logs (okta-export.csv), MFA enforcement dashboard export.
- Change management (CM): PR-based deployments, timestamped approvals, rollback runbooks. Evidence: PRs (GH PR IDs), CI pipeline logs, canary rollout notes (console traces).
- Logging & monitoring (LM): centralized ELK (now hosted as Observability), retention policy, alerting runbooks, tracer sampling config. Evidence: index retention config, PagerDuty incident records, alert runbooks.
- Incident response (IR): incident playbook, tabletop notes, post-incident report templates. Evidence: latest incident report (#INC-2026-02), tabletop attendance sheet.
- Vendor mgmt (VM): inventory of third parties, risk tiering (high/med/low), contracts with security clauses. Evidence: vendor inventory spreadsheet, contract excerpts.

Mini-risk scoring (subjective):
- Access controls: MED (we have SSO+MFA but some legacy service accounts in projects)
- Change mgmt: LOW-MED (good PR trail, but manual approvals for infra changes are inconsistent)
- Logging: MED-HIGH (retention sometimes below ask, sampling skews for low-latency services)
- IR: LOW (playbooks exist but needs regular drills)
- Vendor mgmt: MED (inventory present but not re-assessed quarterly)

Draft evidence checklist (what I'd collect first pass):
- IAM: policy exports, list of service accounts, recent admin sessions (last 90d)
- SSO: org-wide login report + MFA enforcement screenshot
- PRs: top 10 infra PRs from audit window (IDs + approvers)
- CI: build/release artifacts + timestamps for deploys
- Logs: retention policy screenshot, a sample of logs for a 7-day slice (anonymized)
- Backup: export of backup schedule + last successful restore test note
- Incidents: most recent postmortem + evidence of action items closed
- Vendors: inventory CSV + contract redactions highlighting security clauses

Notes-to-self: quick mapping ideas/shortcuts
- For service accounts: map to jira ticket when created (save as label) — quick script could tag accounts with ticket id
- Use GH PR titles with prefix infra/ or ops/ — easy filter for evidence collection
- Ask observability to produce a "retention snapshot" API that returns per-index retention (saves manual screenshots)
- For private deployments, add a one-line boundary note: "private deployment = customer-managed compute & KMS; Redwood traces control plane ops only"

Things to draft this week (prioritized):
- Short policy blurb for ephemeral access (owner: Ellie) — due 2026-02-25
- Evidence pullbook (how-to) with quick commands and where to export artifacts (owner: Dion) — v0 due 2026-03-01
- Vendor inventory tidy-up + risk re-tier (owner: Maya) — due 2026-03-04

Low-effort automation ideas (notes):
- GH search query saved that returns all PRs in audit window with label infra/deploy and outputs CSV (can be used by auditor).
- Small lambda to pull SSO login summary for date range (csv) and drop into shared evidence bucket.
- Script to scan service-account age and produce slack report to owners (nudge to rotate/delete).

Sticky bits / gotchas to flag to manager:
- Private/on-prem customers: evidence boundaries vary — auditors will ask for signed boundary agreements. Get legal to pre-approve.
- Some telemetry is sampled to save cost. Need to enumerate sampling rates per service (and justify to auditor).
- Backups: cross-region copy logs are sometimes in a separate project — need to include that project in evidence pull scope.

Random fragments (brainstorm style):
- "evidence-by-route" view: tie each API route (console, embeddings, generation) to minimal evidence set (auth log, deploy PR, runtime metrics) — could speed up a scoped audit.
- small eval: could we produce a "SOC2 quick-report" CLI that takes service name + date range -> zips evidence? MVP: 2 services.

References / helpful links (placeholders):
- Confluence: /spaces/SEC/pages/1274/ SOC2+Audit+playbook (internal)
- Jira: SEC-489 (evidence automation task)
- Slack thread: #trust-ops pinned "evidence cookbook"

Next immediate action: assemble evidence pullbook skeleton, email Ellie & Maya to divide initial artifacts.

-- dion
